Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 33, verse 38–40:

(p-392) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿There is no blame upon the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him﴾. Qatadah said: "In what Allah has permitted him of women."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The sunnah of Allah﴾ is in the accusative as an infinitive (maṣdar), because the meaning of "There is no blame upon the Prophet" is: Allah has laid down a broad sunnah in which there is no blame. And "those who passed on before" are the prophets. So the meaning is that the sunnah of Allah regarding the widening (of latitude) for Muhammad in what He ordained for him is like His sunnah regarding the earlier prophets. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: "Thus is the sunnah of Allah regarding the prophets, such as Dawud, for he had a hundred wives, and Sulayman had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines." (p-393) ﴿And the command of Allah is a decree determined﴾, that is, a decree decreed. Ibn Qutaybah said: "The sunnah of Allah in those who passed on before" means: there is no blame upon anyone regarding what has not been forbidden to him.

Then Allah praised the prophets with His saying: ﴿Who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and fear none except Allah﴾, that is, they do not fear the blame of people or their words regarding what has been made lawful for them. The rest of the verse has already been explained [al-Nisa': 6].

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾. The exegetes said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Zaynab, people said: "Muhammad has married the wife of his son." So this verse was revealed. The meaning: he is not a father to Zayd, so that his wife would be forbidden to him. ﴿But he is the Messenger of Allah﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever reads it in the accusative, the meaning is "but he was the Messenger of Allah, and he was the Seal of the Prophets"; whoever reads it in the nominative, the meaning is "but he is the Messenger of Allah"; whoever reads "khatam" with a kasra on the ta', its meaning is "and he sealed the Prophets"; and whoever reads it with a fatha, the meaning is "the last of the Prophets." Ibn 'Abbas said: He means: if I had not sealed the prophets with him, I would have made for him a son who would be a prophet after him.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 33, verse 41–44:

(p-396) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Remember Allah with much remembrance﴾. Mujahid said: it is that one never forgets Him at all. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: it is said, "﴿remembrance much﴾" with the five prayers. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it is tasbih (glorification), tahmid (praising), tahlil (saying La ilaha illa Allah) and takbir (saying Allahu akbar) in every state. Abu Hurayra has narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Your Lord says: I am with My servant when he remembers Me and his lips move with Me."

(p-397) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And glorify Him morning and evening﴾. Abu Ubayda said: al-asil is what is between the 'asr (afternoon) and the night. Among the exegetes there are two views regarding this glorification.

The first: it is the prayer, and those who hold this view agree that what is meant by glorifying "in the morning" is the Fajr prayer.

They differ about the prayer of al-asil into three views. The first: it is the 'Asr prayer, (p-398) said by Abu al-'Aliya and Qatada. The second: it is the Zuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers, said by Ibn al-Sa'ib. The third: it is the Zuhr and 'Asr prayers, said by Muqatil.

The second view: it is glorification by the tongue, which is the saying "Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah," said by Mujahid.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He it is who sends blessings upon you, and His angels﴾. Regarding Allah's blessing upon us there are five views.

The first: it is His mercy, said by al-Hasan. The second: it is His forgiveness, said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. The third: it is His praise (of them), said by Abu al-'Aliya. The fourth: it is His honour, said by Sufyan. The fifth: it is His blessing, said by Abu Ubayda.

Regarding the blessing of the angels there are two views.

The first: it is their supplication, said by Abu al-'Aliya. The second: it is their seeking forgiveness, said by Muqatil.

Regarding "darknesses" and "light" here there are three views.

The first: they are misguidance and guidance, said by Ibn Zayd. The second: they are faith and disbelief, said by Muqatil. The third: they are Paradise and Hellfire, related by al-Mawardi.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Their greeting﴾. The (ه) and (م) refer to the believers.

As for the (ه) in His saying: ﴿on the day they meet Him﴾, there are two views regarding it.

The first: it refers back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then there are three views within this. The first: its meaning is: their greeting from Allah on the day they meet Him is "Salam (peace)." Suhayb narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that Allah sends peace upon the people of Paradise. The second: their greeting from the angels on the day they meet Allah is "Salam," (p-399) said by Muqatil. Abu Hamza al-Thumali said: the angels greet them with peace on the Day of Resurrection and give them glad tidings when they come out of their graves. The third: their greeting among themselves on the day they meet their Lord is "Salam," which is that some of them greet one another with peace; this was mentioned by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

The second view: the (ه) refers back to the Angel of Death, which has been mentioned earlier in the mention of the angels. Ibn Mas'ud said: when the Angel of Death comes to seize the soul of a believer, he says to him: "Your Lord conveys to you His peace." Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said regarding His saying: ﴿their greeting on the day they meet Him﴾: it is the Angel of Death; no believer's soul is seized except that he greets him with peace. As for ﴿the noble reward﴾, it is the goodness in Paradise.

The first: they are misguidance and guidance, said by Ibn Zayd. The second: they are faith and disbelief, said by Muqatil. The third: they are Paradise and Hellfire, related by al-Mawardi.

As for the (ه) in His saying: ﴿on the day they meet Him﴾, there are two views regarding it.

The first: it refers back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then there are three views within this. The first: its meaning is: their greeting from Allah on the day they meet Him is "Salam (peace)." Suhayb narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that Allah sends peace upon the people of Paradise. The second: their greeting from the angels on the day they meet Allah is "Salam," (p-399) said by Muqatil. Abu Hamza al-Thumali said: the angels greet them with peace on the Day of Resurrection and give them glad tidings when they come out of their graves. The third: their greeting among themselves on the day they meet their Lord is "Salam," which is that some of them greet one another with peace; this was mentioned by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

The second view: the (ه) refers back to the Angel of Death, which has been mentioned earlier in the mention of the angels. Ibn Mas'ud said: when the Angel of Death comes to seize the soul of a believer, he says to him: "Your Lord conveys to you His peace." Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said regarding His saying: ﴿their greeting on the day they meet Him﴾: it is the Angel of Death; no believer's soul is seized except that he greets him with peace. As for ﴿the noble reward﴾, it is the goodness in Paradise.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 33, verse 41–44:

(p-396) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Remember Allah with much remembrance﴾. Mujahid said: it is that one never forgets Him at all. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: it is said, "﴿remembrance much﴾" with the five prayers. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it is tasbih (glorification), tahmid (praising), tahlil (saying La ilaha illa Allah) and takbir (saying Allahu akbar) in every state. Abu Hurayra has narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Your Lord says: I am with My servant when he remembers Me and his lips move with Me."

(p-397) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And glorify Him morning and evening﴾. Abu Ubayda said: al-asil is what is between the 'asr (afternoon) and the night. Among the exegetes there are two views regarding this glorification.

The first: it is the prayer, and those who hold this view agree that what is meant by glorifying "in the morning" is the Fajr prayer.

They differ about the prayer of al-asil into three views. The first: it is the 'Asr prayer, (p-398) said by Abu al-'Aliya and Qatada. The second: it is the Zuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers, said by Ibn al-Sa'ib. The third: it is the Zuhr and 'Asr prayers, said by Muqatil.

The second view: it is glorification by the tongue, which is the saying "Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah," said by Mujahid.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He it is who sends blessings upon you, and His angels﴾. Regarding Allah's blessing upon us there are five views.

The first: it is His mercy, said by al-Hasan. The second: it is His forgiveness, said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. The third: it is His praise (of them), said by Abu al-'Aliya. The fourth: it is His honour, said by Sufyan. The fifth: it is His blessing, said by Abu Ubayda.

Regarding the blessing of the angels there are two views.

The first: it is their supplication, said by Abu al-'Aliya. The second: it is their seeking forgiveness, said by Muqatil.

Regarding "darknesses" and "light" here there are three views.

The first: they are misguidance and guidance, said by Ibn Zayd. The second: they are faith and disbelief, said by Muqatil. The third: they are Paradise and Hellfire, related by al-Mawardi.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Their greeting﴾. The (ه) and (م) refer to the believers.

As for the (ه) in His saying: ﴿on the day they meet Him﴾, there are two views regarding it.

The first: it refers back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then there are three views within this. The first: its meaning is: their greeting from Allah on the day they meet Him is "Salam (peace)." Suhayb narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that Allah sends peace upon the people of Paradise. The second: their greeting from the angels on the day they meet Allah is "Salam," (p-399) said by Muqatil. Abu Hamza al-Thumali said: the angels greet them with peace on the Day of Resurrection and give them glad tidings when they come out of their graves. The third: their greeting among themselves on the day they meet their Lord is "Salam," which is that some of them greet one another with peace; this was mentioned by Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi.

The second view: the (ه) refers back to the Angel of Death, which has been mentioned earlier in the mention of the angels. Ibn Mas'ud said: when the Angel of Death comes to seize the soul of a believer, he says to him: "Your Lord conveys to you His peace." Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said regarding His saying: ﴿their greeting on the day they meet Him﴾: it is the Angel of Death; no believer's soul is seized except that he greets him with peace. As for ﴿the noble reward﴾, it is the goodness in Paradise.

(p-400) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness﴾, i.e., over your nation with regard to conveying the message, ﴿and a bringer of good news﴾ of Paradise to whoever believes you, ﴿and a warner﴾, i.e., one who warns of the Fire to whoever denies you. ﴿And as one who invites to Allah﴾, i.e., to His Oneness and obedience, ﴿by His permission﴾, i.e., by His command, not that you did it of your own accord. ﴿And as a illuminating lamp﴾, i.e., you are for those who follow you a "lamp" (sirajan), meaning like a lamp shining in darkness by which one is guided.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that for them is from Allah a great bounty﴾, which is Paradise. Jabir ibn Abd Allah said: When His saying was revealed, ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear victory﴾ and the verses that follow [al-Fath], the Companions said: "Congratulations to you, Messenger of Allah, but what about us?" So this verse was revealed.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers﴾ has already been discussed at the beginning of the surah.

His saying, Exalted is He: "And leave their harm." The scholars said: its meaning is: do not repay them for it. ﴿And rely upon Allah﴾ for sufficiency against their evil. This verse is abrogated by the verse of the sword.

[p-401] Allah the Exalted says: ﴿When you marry believing women﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "nakahtum" is "tazawwajtum" (you wed). The meaning of ﴿you touch them﴾ is "you approach them." Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited "tamassuhunna" with an alif (tamasshuhunna, "you have intimacy with them").

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So you have no waiting period for them to count﴾. The scholars agreed that if the divorce occurs before intercourse (masis) and seclusion (khalwa, being alone together), there is no waiting period ('idda). According to us, seclusion requires a waiting period and confirms the bridal gift (sadaq), contrary to al-Shafi'i.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So provide for them﴾. It refers to the one for whom no bridal gift (mahr) has been specified, based on His saying in al-Baqarah (2:236): ﴿or you specify for them a portion﴾. We have already explained provision (mut'ah) there. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Qatadah used to say that this verse is abrogated (mansukha, naskh) by His saying: ﴿then half of what you specified﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:237].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿and release them with a graceful release﴾, meaning without harm. Qatadah said: it is divorcing her while she is in a state of purity without having had intercourse. Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la said: the more apparent view is that this release (tasrih) is not a divorce, because He has already mentioned divorce. Rather, it clarifies that he has no authority over her and that he must free her from his hand and his bonds.

Section

The scholars differed concerning one who says: "If I marry such-and-such a woman, then she is divorced," and then he marries her. According to us, she is not divorced. This is also the view of Ibn 'Abbas, 'A'isha, and al-Shafi'i. Our companions used this verse as evidence, since He made divorce after marriage. Simak ibn al-Fadl said: marriage is a knot and divorce undoes it, so how can it undo a knot that was never tied? With this statement he was judged as a ruler over "San'a'". Abu Hanifah said: the divorce takes effect, so when the marriage occurs it falls. Malik said: it takes effect in the specific case of particular women, namely when it concerns a woman identified by name, and does not take effect in general reference to women. As for when he says: "If I own such-and-such a man, then he is free," there are two reports from Ahmad concerning it.

﴿Indeed We have made lawful for you your wives﴾. Allah mentions the kinds of marriage He made lawful for him, saying: ﴿your wives whom you have given their bridal payments﴾, meaning their dowries (mahr), and these are the women you married with a dowry. ﴿And those whom your right hand possesses﴾, meaning the slave women, ﴿of what Allah has granted you as spoils﴾, meaning what He returned to you from the disbelievers, such as Safiyya and Juwayriya, for he freed them and married them. ﴿And the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts﴾, meaning the women of Quraysh, ﴿and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts﴾, meaning the women of Banu Zuhra, ﴿who have emigrated with you﴾ to Madina.

Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la said: The apparent meaning of this indicates that any woman who did not emigrate with him was not lawful for him to marry. Umm Hani said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed to me, and I excused myself to him with an excuse. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed We have made lawful for you your wives﴾ up to His words ﴿who have emigrated with you﴾." She said: "So I was not lawful for him, because I had not emigrated with him; I was among the freed ones (al-Tulaqa')." From her position, this indicates that restricting him to the emigrant women made the prohibition of those who did not emigrate obligatory.

Some exegetes (mufassirun) mentioned that the condition of emigration in the permission is abrogated (mansukh), but they did not mention its abrogating text (nasikh). Al-Mawardi related two opinions on this. The first: emigration is a condition for the lawfulness of women for him in general. The second: it is a condition for the lawfulness of the relatives mentioned in the verse, but not for unrelated women.

﴿And a believing woman﴾, meaning: and We have made lawful for you a believing woman ﴿if she gives herself﴾ to you, ﴿if the Prophet wishes to marry her﴾, meaning if he prefers to marry her, ﴿exclusively for you﴾, meaning specifically. Al-Zajjaj said: He said ﴿if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾ and did not say "to you," because if He had said "to you," it could have been supposed that this is permissible for someone other than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as it is permissible in the case of the daughters of paternal uncles and paternal aunts. ﴿Exclusively﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal).

The exegetes have three opinions on the meaning of "exclusively":

The first: when a woman gives herself to him, he is not obliged to pay her dowry, unlike other believers. This was said by Anas ibn Malik and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib.

The second: he may marry her without a guardian (wali) and without a dowry, unlike others. This was said by Qatada.

The third: "exclusively for you" means that you alone may own the contract of marriage with her by the wording of gift (hiba), unlike the believers. This is the opinion of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad.

Regarding the woman who gave herself to him, there are several opinions. One is Umm Sharik. The second is Khawla bint Hakim. He did not consummate the marriage with either of them. They mentioned that Layla bint al-Khatim gave herself to him, but he did not accept her. Ibn Abbas said: "There was no woman with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who gave herself to him." It is also related from Ibn Abbas that the woman who gave herself to him was Maymuna bint al-Harith, and from al-Sha'bi that she was Zaynab bint Khuzayma. The first opinion is the most sound.

﴿We have certainly known what We have enjoined upon them﴾, meaning upon the believers other than you, ﴿concerning their wives﴾. There are two opinions on this:

The first: that a man should not exceed four women. This was said by Mujahid.

The second: that a man should not marry a woman except with a guardian, two witnesses, and a dowry. This was said by Qatada.

﴿Or what their right hands possess﴾, meaning: and what We have permitted them of ownership by the right hand, along with the four free wives, without a limited number.

﴿So that there will be no discomfort for you﴾. This contains an inversion (taqdim). The meaning is: We have made lawful for you your wives, up to His words ﴿exclusively for you, apart from the believers﴾, ﴿so that there will be no discomfort for you﴾.

﴿You may postpone whom you will of them﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, and Abu Bakr from Asim read "turji'" with a hamza. Nafi', Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from Asim read it without a hamza. The occasion of revelation was that when the verse of choice (ayat al-takhyir) mentioned earlier was revealed, they feared they would be divorced, so they said: "O Prophet of Allah, grant us from your wealth and yourself whatever you wish, and leave us in our state." Then this verse was revealed. This was said by Abu Razin.

There are four opinions on the meaning of the verse:

The first: you divorce whom you will of your wives, and keep whom you will of your wives. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: you leave off marrying whom you will, and marry from the women of your community whom you will. This was said by al-Hasan.

The third: you set aside whom you will of your wives, so you do not come to her without divorce, and you come to whom you will without setting her aside. This was said by Mujahid.

The fourth: you accept whom you will of the believing women who give themselves, and leave whom you will. This was said by al-Sha'bi and Ikrima.

Most scholars hold that this verse was revealed permitting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to be with his wives as he willed, without the obligation of division (qasma) and equality among them, although he used to make equality among them. Al-Zuhri said: "We do not know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) postponed any one of them, and he gave shelter to all of them until he died." Abu Razin said: "He sheltered Aisha, Umm Salama, Hafsa, and Zaynab, and his division from himself and his wealth among them was equal. He postponed Sawda, Juwayriya, Safiyya, Umm Habiba, and Maymuna, and he would divide for them as he wished. He had intended to separate from them, so they said: 'Divide for us as you wish, and leave us in our state.'" Some said: "He postponed only Sawda, because she gave her day to Aisha, and he died while dividing among eight."

﴿And you may take into your care﴾, meaning: you gather to yourself. ﴿And whoever you desire from those you have set aside﴾, meaning: if you wish to bring to yourself a woman from those you have set aside from the division, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, meaning: there is no inclination for you with reproach or censure. ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted﴾, meaning: that choice which We gave you regarding their companionship is closer to their contentment. The meaning is: when they know that this is a command from Allah, it is more pleasing to their souls. Ibn Muhaysin and Abu Imran al-Jawni read "an tuqirra" with a damma on the ta and a kasra on the qaf, and "u'ina-hunna" with a fatha on the nun.

﴿And they will be pleased with what you give them, all of them﴾, meaning: with what you give them of favor or delay. ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾, meaning the inclination toward some of them. The meaning is: We gave you choice only to ease matters for you.

﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾. All of them read "la yahillu" with a ya', except Abu Amr, who read it with a ta'; the feminine form is not real, but is the feminine of a plural, so both readings are good.

There are three opinions on the phrase ﴿after this﴾:

The first: after your wives whom you gave the choice and who chose Allah and His Messenger. This was said by Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, and others. They are the nine. Thus the permission was restricted to them and forbidden from others. The people of knowledge mentioned that his divorce of Hafsa and his determination to divorce Sawda occurred before the choice.

The second: after what We have made lawful for you. So the permission after his wives was restricted to what was mentioned in His words ﴿Indeed We have made lawful for you your wives﴾ up to His words ﴿exclusively for you﴾. This was said by Ubayy ibn Ka'b and al-Dahhak.

The third: women who are not Muslims are not lawful for you, such as Jewish and Christian and polytheist women, while Muslim women are lawful for you. This was said by Mujahid.

﴿Nor that you exchange them﴾. There are three opinions on this:

The first: that you divorce your wives and exchange them for others. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The second: that you exchange Muslim women for polytheist women. This was said by Mujahid and others.

The third: that you give your wife to a man and take his wife, and this was a custom of the Jahiliyya. This was said by Abu Hurayra and Ibn Zayd.

﴿Except what your right hand possesses﴾, meaning the female slaves.

There are three opinions on the meaning of the statement:

The first: except that you own by captivity (sabi), so it is lawful for you to have intercourse with her, even if she is not from the category which I made lawful for you. Ubayy ibn Ka'b pointed to this, along with others.

The second: except that you come upon a Jewish or Christian woman and have intercourse with her by ownership of the right hand. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Mujahid.

The third: except that you exchange your slave woman for the slave woman of another. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi said: These opinions are permissible, but we do not know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married a Jewish or Christian woman, either by marriage or by ownership of the right hand. He did take Rayhana al-Quraziyya captive, but he did not approach her until she had embraced Islam.

Section

The scholars of abrogation and abrogated texts (naskh) differed on this verse into two opinions.

The first: that it is abrogated by His words ﴿Indeed We have made lawful for you your wives﴾. This is related from Ali, Ibn Abbas, Aisha, Umm Salama, Ali ibn al-Husayn, and al-Dahhak. Aisha said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until women of all the tribes were made lawful for him." Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi said: "She meant the women of all the tribes, both emigrants and non-emigrants."

The second opinion: that it is muhkam (unabrogated, firm); and there are then two opinions on this.

The first: that Allah, the Exalted, rewarded his wives when they chose Him by restricting him to them, so no others were made lawful for him, and this was not abrogated. This was said by al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Abu Umama ibn Sahl, and Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith.

The second: that what is meant by "the women" here is the disbelieving women, and it was not lawful for him to marry a disbeliever. This was said by Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrima, and Jabir ibn Zayd.

﴿Indeed We have made lawful for you your wives﴾. Allah mentions the kinds of marriage He made lawful for him, saying: ﴿your wives whom you have given their bridal payments﴾, meaning their dowries (mahr), and these are the women you married with a dowry. ﴿And those whom your right hand possesses﴾, meaning the slave women, ﴿of what Allah has granted you as spoils﴾, meaning what He returned to you from the disbelievers, such as Safiyya and Juwayriya, for he freed them and married them. ﴿And the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts﴾, meaning the women of Quraysh, ﴿and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts﴾, meaning the women of Banu Zuhra, ﴿who have emigrated with you﴾ to Madina.

Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la said: The apparent meaning of this indicates that any woman who did not emigrate with him was not lawful for him to marry. Umm Hani said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed to me, and I excused myself to him with an excuse. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed We have made lawful for you your wives﴾ up to His words ﴿who have emigrated with you﴾." She said: "So I was not lawful for him, because I had not emigrated with him; I was among the freed ones (al-Tulaqa')." From her position, this indicates that restricting him to the emigrant women made the prohibition of those who did not emigrate obligatory.

Some exegetes (mufassirun) mentioned that the condition of emigration in the permission is abrogated (mansukh), but they did not mention its abrogating text (nasikh). Al-Mawardi related two opinions on this. The first: emigration is a condition for the lawfulness of women for him in general. The second: it is a condition for the lawfulness of the relatives mentioned in the verse, but not for unrelated women.

﴿And a believing woman﴾, meaning: and We have made lawful for you a believing woman ﴿if she gives herself﴾ to you, ﴿if the Prophet wishes to marry her﴾, meaning if he prefers to marry her, ﴿exclusively for you﴾, meaning specifically. Al-Zajjaj said: He said ﴿if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾ and did not say "to you," because if He had said "to you," it could have been supposed that this is permissible for someone other than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as it is permissible in the case of the daughters of paternal uncles and paternal aunts. ﴿Exclusively﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal).

The exegetes have three opinions on the meaning of "exclusively":

The first: when a woman gives herself to him, he is not obliged to pay her dowry, unlike other believers. This was said by Anas ibn Malik and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib.

The second: he may marry her without a guardian (wali) and without a dowry, unlike others. This was said by Qatada.

The third: "exclusively for you" means that you alone may own the contract of marriage with her by the wording of gift (hiba), unlike the believers. This is the opinion of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad.

Regarding the woman who gave herself to him, there are several opinions. One is Umm Sharik. The second is Khawla bint Hakim. He did not consummate the marriage with either of them. They mentioned that Layla bint al-Khatim gave herself to him, but he did not accept her. Ibn Abbas said: "There was no woman with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who gave herself to him." It is also related from Ibn Abbas that the woman who gave herself to him was Maymuna bint al-Harith, and from al-Sha'bi that she was Zaynab bint Khuzayma. The first opinion is the most sound.

The first: that a man should not exceed four women. This was said by Mujahid.

The second: that a man should not marry a woman except with a guardian, two witnesses, and a dowry. This was said by Qatada.

﴿Or what their right hands possess﴾, meaning: and what We have permitted them of ownership by the right hand, along with the four free wives, without a limited number.

﴿So that there will be no discomfort for you﴾. This contains an inversion (taqdim). The meaning is: We have made lawful for you your wives, up to His words ﴿exclusively for you, apart from the believers﴾, ﴿so that there will be no discomfort for you﴾.

﴿You may postpone whom you will of them﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, and Abu Bakr from Asim read "turji'" with a hamza. Nafi', Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from Asim read it without a hamza. The occasion of revelation was that when the verse of choice (ayat al-takhyir) mentioned earlier was revealed, they feared they would be divorced, so they said: "O Prophet of Allah, grant us from your wealth and yourself whatever you wish, and leave us in our state." Then this verse was revealed. This was said by Abu Razin.

There are four opinions on the meaning of the verse:

The first: you divorce whom you will of your wives, and keep whom you will of your wives. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: you leave off marrying whom you will, and marry from the women of your community whom you will. This was said by al-Hasan.

The third: you set aside whom you will of your wives, so you do not come to her without divorce, and you come to whom you will without setting her aside. This was said by Mujahid.

The fourth: you accept whom you will of the believing women who give themselves, and leave whom you will. This was said by al-Sha'bi and Ikrima.

Most scholars hold that this verse was revealed permitting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to be with his wives as he willed, without the obligation of division (qasma) and equality among them, although he used to make equality among them. Al-Zuhri said: "We do not know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) postponed any one of them, and he gave shelter to all of them until he died." Abu Razin said: "He sheltered Aisha, Umm Salama, Hafsa, and Zaynab, and his division from himself and his wealth among them was equal. He had intended to separate from them, so they said: 'Divide for us as you wish, and leave us in our state.'" Some said: "He postponed only Sawda, because she gave her day to Aisha, and he died while dividing among eight."

﴿And you may take into your care﴾, meaning: you gather to yourself. ﴿And whoever you desire from those you have set aside﴾, meaning: if you wish to bring to yourself a woman from those you have set aside from the division, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, meaning: there is no inclination for you with reproach or censure. ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted﴾, meaning: that choice which We gave you regarding their companionship is closer to their contentment. The meaning is: when they know that this is a command from Allah, it is more pleasing to their souls. Ibn Muhaysin and Abu Imran al-Jawni read "an tuqirra" with a damma on the ta and a kasra on the qaf, and "u'ina-hunna" with a fatha on the nun.

﴿And they will be pleased with what you give them, all of them﴾, meaning: with what you give them of favor or delay. ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾, meaning the inclination toward some of them. The meaning is: We gave you choice only to ease matters for you.

﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾. All of them read "la yahillu" with a ya', except Abu Amr, who read it with a ta'; the feminine form is not real, but is the feminine of a plural, so both readings are good.

There are three opinions on the phrase ﴿after this﴾:

The first: after your wives whom you gave the choice and who chose Allah and His Messenger. This was said by Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, and others. They are the nine. Thus the permission was restricted to them and forbidden from others. The people of knowledge mentioned that his divorce of Hafsa and his determination to divorce Sawda occurred before the choice.

The second: after what We have made lawful for you. So the permission after his wives was restricted to what was mentioned in His words ﴿Indeed We have made lawful for you your wives﴾ up to His words ﴿exclusively for you﴾. This was said by Ubayy ibn Ka'b and al-Dahhak.

The third: women who are not Muslims are not lawful for you, such as Jewish and Christian and polytheist women, while Muslim women are lawful for you. This was said by Mujahid.

﴿Nor that you exchange them﴾. There are three opinions on this:

The first: that you divorce your wives and exchange them for others. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The second: that you exchange Muslim women for polytheist women. This was said by Mujahid and others.

The third: that you give your wife to a man and take his wife, and this was a custom of the Jahiliyya. This was said by Abu Hurayra and Ibn Zayd.

﴿Except what your right hand possesses﴾, meaning the female slaves.

(p-412) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet﴾ — the verse. Regarding the occasion of its revelation there are six opinions.

(p-413) The first opinion: Al-Bukhari and Muslim both transmitted it in their Sahihs from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jahsh, he invited the people, and they ate, then sat conversing. He then began as if he were preparing to rise, but they did not rise. When he saw that, he got up, and some of the people got up with him, but three remained seated. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and entered, and found the people still seated, so he went back. Then they got up and departed, and I came and informed the Prophet ﷺ that they had left, so he came and entered, and I went to enter, but he placed the curtain between me and him. And Allah the Exalted revealed this verse."

The second: "Some of the believers used to watch for the food of the Prophet ﷺ, entering upon him before the meal was ready, and then they would eat and not leave. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was harmed by them, so this verse was revealed." This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The third: "Umar ibn al-Khattab said: 'I said, O Messenger of Allah, indeed both the righteous and the wicked enter upon your wives, so if you were to command them to veil themselves...' and the verse of the hijab was revealed." Al-Bukhari transmitted it from the hadith of Anas, and Muslim transmitted it from the hadith of Ibn Umar, both from Umar.

The fourth: "Umar commanded the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to veil, and Zaynab said: 'O son of al-Khattab, you are jealous of us, while revelation descends in our houses?!' So the verse was revealed." This was said by Ibn Mas'ud.

The fifth: "Umar used to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'Veil your wives,' but he would not do so. Then Sawda went out one night, and Umar said: 'We have recognized you, O Sawda'—eager that the hijab be revealed—so the hijab was revealed." Narrated by Ikrimah from Aisha.

(p-415) The sixth: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to eat with some of his companions, and the hand of a man among them touched the hand of Aisha, who was with them, and the Prophet ﷺ disliked that, so the verse of the hijab was revealed." This was said by Mujahid.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿except that you be given leave for a meal﴾, i.e., that you be invited to it, ﴿not waiting for its preparation﴾, i.e., not waiting for it ﴿ina'hu﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the position of "an" is in the accusative; the meaning is: except by being given leave, or for being given leave. "Ghayra" (not) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state; the meaning is: except that you be given leave, not waiting. "Ina'hu" means its being cooked and its becoming ready.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿then disperse﴾, i.e., go out.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿nor lingering for conversation﴾. The meaning: do not enter lingering, i.e., seeking companionship in conversation. That was because they used to sit after eating and converse at length, and that would harm him, and he was shy to tell them "Get up." So Allah taught them good manners. This is His saying: ﴿And Allah is not shy of the truth﴾, i.e., He does not refrain from making clear to you what the truth is. ﴿And when you ask them for an article, ask them from behind a screen﴾, i.e., any item to be used and benefited from, of household utensils. ﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾, i.e., your asking them for goods from behind a screen is purer, ﴿for your hearts and their hearts﴾, from suspicion.

(p-416) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾, i.e., it is not permissible for you to harm him in any matter. Abu Ubayda said: "Kana" is among the superfluous particles, and the meaning is: it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah. ﴿Nor to marry his wives after him, ever﴾. Ata transmitted from Ibn Abbas that a man among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dies, I will marry Aisha," so Allah revealed what He revealed. Muqatil claimed that this man was Talha ibn Ubayd Allah.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, that is, with Allah, an enormous sin﴾, meaning the marrying of the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, i.e., a sin of great punishment.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 33, verse 54–55:

(p-417) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Whether you disclose something or conceal it﴾. It was said: it was revealed concerning what the speaker expressed: "If the Messenger of Allah dies, I will marry ʿĀʾisha."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿there is no blame upon them concerning their fathers﴾. The exegetes said: when the verse of hijab was revealed, the fathers, the sons, and the relatives said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Are we also to speak to them from behind a screen?" So Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿there is no blame upon them concerning their fathers﴾, meaning: in that they may see them and not veil themselves from them, up to His saying: ﴿nor their women﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: this means the women of the believers, because the women of the Jews and the Christians describe the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to their husbands if they see them.

If it is asked: why were the paternal uncle and the maternal uncle not mentioned? Concerning this there are two answers.

(p-418) One: because a woman is lawful to their sons, so it was disliked that she should remove her head-covering in the presence of her paternal uncle and maternal uncle, since they would describe her to their sons. This is the saying of al-Shaʿbi and ʿIkrima.

The second: because they take the place of the parents, so they were not mentioned. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

As for His saying: ﴿nor what their right hands possess﴾, there are two views:

One: that it means female slaves only, not male slaves. This was said by Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab.

The second: that it is general, covering both male and female slaves. Ibn Zayd said: the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not veil themselves from the male slaves. The explanation of this has already passed in Surat al-Nur (24:31).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And fear Allah﴾, meaning: lest anyone other than these see you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Witness﴾, meaning: nothing is hidden from Him.

The exegetes said: when the verse of hijab was revealed, the fathers, the sons, and the relatives said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Are we also to speak to them from behind a screen?" So Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿there is no blame upon them concerning their fathers﴾, meaning: in that they may see them and not veil themselves from them, up to His saying: ﴿nor their women﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: this means the women of the believers, because the women of the Jews and the Christians describe the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to their husbands if they see them.

If it is asked: why were the paternal uncle and the maternal uncle not mentioned? Concerning this there are two answers.

(p-418) One: because a woman is lawful to their sons, so it was disliked that she should remove her head-covering in the presence of her paternal uncle and maternal uncle, since they would describe her to their sons. This is the saying of al-Shaʿbi and ʿIkrima.

The second: because they take the place of the parents, so they were not mentioned. This was said by al-Zajjaj.

As for His saying: ﴿nor what their right hands possess﴾, there are two views:

One: that it means female slaves only, not male slaves. This was said by Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab.

The second: that it is general, covering both male and female slaves. Ibn Zayd said: the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not veil themselves from the male slaves. The explanation of this has already passed in Surat al-Nur (24:31).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And fear Allah﴾, meaning: lest anyone other than these see you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Witness﴾, meaning: nothing is hidden from Him.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 33, verse 56–58:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾. There are statements regarding the blessing of Allah and the blessing of the angels, which have already been mentioned in this surah [al-Ahzab: 43].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, invoke blessings upon him and greet him with peace﴾. Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah said: "We said: O Messenger of Allah, we have known the greeting of peace upon you, so how is the blessing upon you?" He said: "Say: 'O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon the family [of] Ibrahim. Indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family [of] Ibrahim. Indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.'" (p-419) Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim. As for his saying, "We have known the greeting upon you": it refers to what is said in the tashahhud, "Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings." Ibn al-Sa'ib held that the meaning of "taslim" is: submit to what he commands you.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger﴾. The scholars differed concerning who it was revealed about, in three statements.

First: it concerns those who criticized the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he took Safiyyah bint Huyayy. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

Second: it was revealed concerning the image-makers (al-musawwirin). This was said by 'Ikrimah.

Third: it concerns the polytheists, the Jews and the Christians, who attributed a son to Allah, denied His Messenger, wounded his face, broke his incisor, and said: "Madman, poet, sorcerer, liar." The meaning of harming Allah is: describing Him with what is far removed from Him, and disobeying Him; and their being cursed in this world is by killing and exile, and in the Hereafter by the Fire.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women﴾. Concerning the occasion of its revelation there are four statements.

First: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab saw a girl displaying herself, so he struck her and stopped what he saw of her adornment. She went to her family complaining, and they came out to him and harmed him, so this verse was revealed. Related by 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas.

Second: that it was revealed concerning the fornicators who used to walk in the streets of Madinah, following women when they went out at night to attend to their needs. They would see a woman, approach her and grope her. They were only harming the slave-women, but slave-women could not be distinguished from free women, so they complained of that to their husbands, who mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this verse was revealed. This was said by al-Suddi.

Third: that it was revealed concerning those who spoke about 'A'ishah and Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal with the slander. This was said by al-Dahhak.

Fourth: that some of the hypocrites harmed 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, and this verse was revealed. This was said by Muqatil.

The exegetes said: the meaning of the verse is: they accuse them of what is not in them.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 33, verses 59–62:

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾ up to the end of the verse. The occasion of its revelation: the wicked men used to harass women when they went out at night. When they saw a woman wearing a veil (qina'), they left her alone and said, "This is a free woman." But when they saw her without a veil, they said, "This is a slave-girl," and they harassed her. So this verse was revealed. This was related by al-Suddi.

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿They should draw their outer garments over themselves﴾. Ibn Qutayba said: they should wear outer wraps (ardiya). Others said: they should cover their heads and faces so that it may be known that they are free women. ﴿That is more suitable﴾, meaning more fitting and closer, ﴿that they will be recognized﴾ as free women, ﴿and not be harmed﴾.

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist﴾, meaning from their hypocrisy, ﴿and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning immorality, and they are the fornicators, ﴿and the agitators in the city﴾ who spread falsehood and lies, saying: "The enemy has come upon you," and "Your expeditions have been slain and defeated." ﴿We will surely incite you against them﴾, meaning We will empower you over them by commanding you to fight them. The exegetes said: he was indeed incited against them, and it was said to him: (p-423) "Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites" [al-Tawba: 73, al-Tahrim: 9]. He also said on a Friday: "Get out of the mosque, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite; stand up, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite." ﴿Then they will not remain your neighbors therein﴾, meaning in the city, ﴿except briefly﴾ until they perish, ﴿cursed﴾, which is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal); meaning: they will not be your neighbors except while they are cursed. ﴿Wherever they are found﴾, meaning wherever they are met and overtaken, ﴿they will be seized and killed with slaughter﴾. The meaning of the statement is a command, that is, this is the ruling concerning them. ﴿The way of Allah﴾, meaning: He has established for those who oppose the prophets and spread agitation against them that this be done to them.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 33, verse 63–68:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The people ask you about the Hour﴾. ʿUrwa said: The one who asked him about it was ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And what will make you know?﴾ That is: what will inform you of the matter of the Hour and when it will occur? The meaning is: you do not know that. Then He said: ﴿Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾

If it is said: Why did He not say "qarība" (near, feminine)? There are three answers to this.

The first: He intended the adverbial sense (of time). Had He intended the attribute of the Hour itself, He would have said "qarība." This is the view of Abu ʿUbayda. The second: the meaning refers to the Resurrection, or to the coming of the Hour. The third: the feminine form of "al-sāʿa" (the Hour) is not a true feminine. Al-Zajjaj mentioned these two.

As for what follows, its wording has already been explained (al-Baqara: 159; al-Nisāʾ: 10; al-Isrāʾ: 97).

As for His saying: ﴿And we obeyed the Messenger﴾, al-Zajjaj said: The preferred practice is to pause with an alif, because the endings of the verses and their closing rhymes function like the endings of verses of poetry. They were addressed with what they understand of connected speech, so that the pause with an added letter indicates that the speech is complete. We have already pointed to this in His saying: ﴿the assumptions﴾ (al-Aḥzāb: 1).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿We obeyed our leaders and our elders﴾. That is: our nobles and our great ones. Muqatil said: They are the ones who fed (the army) at the Battle of Badr. All of them read ﴿sādatanā﴾ in the singular, except Ibn ʿĀmir, who read "sādātinā" in the plural with a kasra on the tā'. Al-Mufaḍḍal and Yaʿqub agreed with him, except Abu Ḥatim. ﴿And they misled us from the way﴾, that is: from the way of guidance. ﴿Our Lord, give them﴾ meaning the leaders ﴿double punishment﴾, that is: double our punishment. ﴿And curse them with a great curse﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read "kathīran" with the thāʾ. ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read "kabīran" with the bāʾ. Abu ʿAli said: "Kathra" (abundance) is more fitting to repeated instances than "kibar" (greatness).

If it is said: Why did He not say "qarība" (near, feminine)? There are three answers to this.

The first: He intended the adverbial sense (of time). Had He intended the attribute of the Hour itself, He would have said "qarība." This is the view of Abu ʿUbayda. The second: the meaning refers to the Resurrection, or to the coming of the Hour. The third: the feminine form of "al-sāʿa" (the Hour) is not a true feminine. Al-Zajjaj mentioned these two.

As for what follows, its wording has already been explained (al-Baqara: 159; al-Nisāʾ: 10; al-Isrāʾ: 97).

As for His saying: ﴿And we obeyed the Messenger﴾, al-Zajjaj said: The preferred practice is to pause with an alif, because the endings of the verses and their closing rhymes function like the endings of verses of poetry. They were addressed with what they understand of connected speech, so that the pause with an added letter indicates that the speech is complete. We have already pointed to this in His saying: ﴿the assumptions﴾ (al-Aḥzāb: 1).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿We obeyed our leaders and our elders﴾. That is: our nobles and our great ones. Muqatil said: They are the ones who fed (the army) at the Battle of Badr. All of them read ﴿sādatanā﴾ in the singular, except Ibn ʿĀmir, who read "sādātinā" in the plural with a kasra on the tā'. Al-Mufaḍḍal and Yaʿqub agreed with him, except Abu Ḥatim. ﴿And they misled us from the way﴾, that is: from the way of guidance. ﴿Our Lord, give them﴾ meaning the leaders ﴿double punishment﴾, that is: double our punishment. ﴿And curse them with a great curse﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read "kathīran" with the thāʾ. ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read "kabīran" with the bāʾ. Abu ʿAli said: "Kathra" (abundance) is more fitting to repeated instances than "kibar" (greatness).

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 33, verse 69–71:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do not be like those who harmed Moses﴾, meaning: do not harm Muhammad as the Children of Israel harmed Moses, lest there befall you what befell them.

(p-425) Concerning what they harmed Moses with, there are four opinions.

The first: they said, "He has a swollen testicle (adar)." One day he went to bathe and placed his garment on a rock, and the rock fled with his garment, so he went out in pursuit of it. They saw him and said, "By God, there is nothing wrong with him." The hadith is well known in all the Sahih collections from the narration of Abu Hurayra, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ); I have mentioned it with its chain in "al-Mughni" and "al-Hada'iq." Ibn Qutayba said: the adar is one with a large pair of testicles.

The second: Moses ascended the mountain with Harun, and Harun died. The Children of Israel said, "You killed him," and so they harmed him with this accusation. God, exalted is He, commanded the angels, and they carried him until they passed by him over the Children of Israel, and the angels spoke of his death until the Children of Israel knew that he had died, and God cleared him of that. This was said by Ali, peace be upon him.

(p-426) The third: Qarun hired a prostitute to accuse Moses publicly before an assembly of the Children of Israel, but God protected her and cleared Moses of that. This was said by Abu al-Aliya.

The fourth: they accused him of sorcery and madness, related by al-Mawardi.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he was honourable (wajihan) in the sight of God﴾. Ibn Abbas said: he was favoured (hazziyyan) with God, who would not ask Him for anything without Him giving it to him. We have explained the meaning of wajih in (Al 'Imran: 45). Ibn Mas'ud, al-A'mash and Abu Haywa read: "wa-kana 'abdan li-llah" (and he was a servant of God), with tanwin on 'abdan, and a kasra on the lam.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And speak words of rectitude﴾. Concerning it there are four opinions.

(p-427) The first: correct (sawaban), said by Ibn Abbas. The second: truthful (sadiqan), said by al-Hasan. The third: just (adlan), said by al-Suddi. The fourth: direct (qasdan), said by Ibn Qutayba.

Then, concerning the intended meaning of this saying, there are three opinions.

The first: that it is "There is no god but God," said by Ibn Abbas and Ikrima. The second: that it is justice in all sayings and deeds, said by Qatada. The third: concerning the matter of Zaynab and Zayd, and do not attribute to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) what is not fitting, said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He will set right your deeds for you﴾. Concerning it there are two opinions.

One: He will accept your good deeds, said by Ibn Abbas. The second: He will purify your deeds, said by Muqatil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then he has indeed achieved a great achievement﴾, meaning: he attained good and gained it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 33, verses 72–73:

God's words, ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust﴾, have two interpretations.

One: it refers to the obligations (al-fara'id). God offered them to the heavens, the earth and the mountains. If they fulfilled them, they would be rewarded; if they neglected them, they would be punished. They disliked this. He offered them to Adam, and he accepted them with what they entail. This was related by Ibn Abi Talha from Ibn Abbas. Sa'id ibn Jubayr likewise said: The Trust was offered to Adam and it was said to him: "Will you take it with what it entails? If you obey, I will forgive you, and if you disobey, I will punish you." He said: "I accept." It was no more than the time between the afternoon prayer and sunset before he committed the sin. Among those who held that it refers to the obligations were Qatada, al-Dahhak and the majority (al-Jumhur).

Two: it is the trust that people place in one another. Al-Suddi related from his shaykhs that when Adam wanted to perform the Hajj, he said to the heaven: "Guard my son with the trust." It refused. He said the same to the earth, and it refused. He said it to the mountains, and they refused. Then he said it to Qabil, and he said: "Yes. Go and come back, and you will find your family as pleasing to you." When Adam set out, Qabil killed Habil. Adam returned and found that his son had killed his brother. This is what God, Mighty and Majestic, refers to in His words: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust﴾ up to His words ﴿and man undertook it﴾, meaning the son of Adam, and he did not uphold it.

Ibn Qutayba related from some of the exegetes that when Adam's death approached, he said: "O Lord, who will succeed me after me?" It was said to him: "Present your succession to all of creation." He presented it, and each of them refused it except for his own offspring.

As for the meaning of offering the Trust to the heavens and the earth, the exegetes have two views.

One: God endowed these entities with intellect, gave them understanding of His address, and enabled them to answer when He offered it to them. His words, "I will come" (ʾabayna, "they refused"), did not signify opposition. Rather, they refused out of awe and fear, because the offering was an option and not a compulsion. ﴿And they feared﴾, meaning they were afraid, ﴿of it﴾, that they would not fulfill it and would thus incur punishment. This is the view of the majority.

Two: the verse means: We offered the Trust to the people of the heavens, the people of the earth and the people of the mountains, meaning the angels. This was stated by al-Hasan.

As for the meaning of "man" (al-insan), there are four views. First, it is Adam, according to the majority. Second, it is Qabil, according to al-Suddi. Third, it is the disbeliever and the hypocrite, according to al-Hasan. Fourth, it is all of humankind, according to Tha'lab.

God's words, ﴿Indeed he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾, have three interpretations.

One: he was a wrongdoer to himself, deceived regarding his Lord's command. This was stated by Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak.

Two: he was a wrongdoer to himself, ignorant of the outcome of his affair. This was stated by Mujahid.

Three: he was a wrongdoer by disobeying his Lord, ignorant of the punishment for breaching the trust. This was stated by Ibn al-Sa'ib.

Al-Zajjaj mentioned an interpretation of the verse that differs from most of the views, and he stated that it agrees with the exegesis. He said: God entrusted the children of Adam with what He made obligatory upon them of obedience to Him, and He entrusted the heavens, the earth and the mountains with obedience to Him and submission to Him. As for the heavens and the earth, they said: ﴿We come willingly﴾ (41:11). He informed us that some stones descend out of fear of God, and that the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains and the angels prostrate to God. God, the Exalted, made us aware that the heavens and the earth did not bear the Trust, because they fulfilled it. Fulfilling it means obeying God and abstaining from disobeying Him. Whoever betrays the Trust has indeed borne it, and likewise whoever commits a sin has borne the sin. Al-Hasan likewise said: ﴿and man undertook it﴾, meaning the disbeliever and the hypocrite undertook it, that is, they betrayed it and did not obey. As for one who obeys, it is not said of him that he was a wrongdoer, ignorant.

God's words, ﴿so that God may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and the polytheist women, and that God may turn in mercy toward the believing men and the believing women﴾. Ibn Qutayba said: The meaning is: We offered this so that the hypocrisy of the hypocrite and the polytheism of the polytheist would become manifest, and God would punish them, and so that the faith of the believers would become manifest, and God would turn to them, that is, return to them with mercy and forgiveness if any shortcoming in acts of obedience occurred from them.
